But whenever markets want a correction people just blindly point to China with memory or optics while ignoring what's actually occurring with demand imbalances + LTAs spanning many years and constantly extending.

Sure... Random train of thoughts on markets now, optics like $LITE / memory + $IREN / Anthropic. 

On Memory: 

- Demand visibility on $MU / Samsung / SK Hynix extend into 2030-2031. 

Samsung has LTAs covering 70% of their capacity into 2031 (likely with SK Hynix type price floors)... and their operating profit is already absurd.  

There's a consensus that shortage in 2027 will be much more severe than 2026... Even $SNDK expends gross margins to exceed 80% entering 2030. 

You're going to hear Acer and other CEOs that want memory prices to go down cite bear cases like CXMT/YMTC, and Chinese players. 

But just looking at supply procurement that $NVDA is doing + hyperscalers, demand visibility is absurd for the next 5 years. And by that time, cumulative FCF coming in from these take/pay + pricing floor contracts might exceed some of their entire marketcaps so it feels like there's some baseline.  

Near-term is always volatile (IV dropped a ton across $EWY to $DRAM to $MU), so people with call options likely got nuked, along with underlying prices. 

But if Samsung is 3x 2027E, has 5 year LTAs with 70% of capacity committed from hyperscalers, and price floors, it's kinda hard to see these names suffer a sustained crash...   

For optics: 

- $LITE is literally sold out into 2029, starting discussions into 2030.  With demand visibility lasting into 2031… with hyperscalers largely funding the capacity buildout.  

Their 2028 Greensboro fab expansion was ~$5B in UHP laser capacity revenue alone, yet it’s basically allocated toward $NVDA (50%+ with options for more) and co from channel checks. 

Existing supply chain bottlenecks are extremely severe as optical content/XPU skyrockets entering 2027-2028.

So everything from DSPs/TIAs, photodiodes, lasers, InP/SOI substrates, wafers (epi, SOI, etc) are expected to go brrr. 

And what does that imply to anyone else with enormous amounts of capacity coming online like $AAOI + $SIVE + $MTSI capacity expansion in 2027? Or other players like Sumitomo / Furukawa? 

But again it's not quite the same situation as memory since the BOM % is extremely low in a cluster... If micron/samsung raised another 2000% hyperscalers would go bankrupt. But doing that for InP substrates seems possible. Or a 100% increase on CW laser content. 

I actually thought $LITE was overvalued at $100B+ MC, relative to capacity expansion on your smaller optical players to their respective MCs. So I chose to position accordingly (But lumentum does deserve premiums for demand visibility). 

For the companies leading the charge like $NVDA / $AVGO / $MRVL:

- Nvidia has 70% forward revenue growth FY2028 which is supply constrained growth. 
- Broadcom 100% Y/Y for 2027/2028 which is also supply constrained growth. 
- Marvell FY2031 upgraded guidance to $70B-$90B from $46B analyst projections... 

They all seem to be very happy.... and read through on demand for next 2-3 years is enormous (also echoing what $INTC CEO said today on the panel with $AVGO CEO).  

So you have overwhelming growth on memory + photonics + from the leaders... But the nuance is not everything in the AI supply chain get the same economic benefit. 

HBM/Laser/CPU/MLCC and other players in the bottlenecks look to be printing money. And seem to be the largest beneficiaries of the current bottlenecks. 

Test players are also getting price hikes + capacity allocated by players like $NVDA, but economic impact seems a tad lower than other players since forward P/E for many I modeled were still in the 45x+ range even if you hiked prices like 10-30%. 

As for capex intensive players... there's some like $IREN ($25-30B for 2027) that despite a deal with Anthropic ended up dropping.  I don't think markets seem to appreciate players spending a lot of money + ongoing financing (think they're like halfway through their $6B ATM). 

Just some hopium for $IREN investors, $NBIS also signed a deal with $META at the start of the year (but markets didn't care at all, since Nebius dropped to ~$70-80 at the lowest point?). 

But did 6 months later, as the time to revenue inflection gets closer and you're past the ATM/capex window, markets would likely care more. 

I don't think it's irrational but at the same time, the fundamentals have improved from Mirantis acquisition to others. I also think it was known for awhile it was either OpenAI/Anthropic from CEO comments earlier too? 

But either way to be a more risk-off environment where funds seem to be rotating to larger names as a flight to safety.

$CRWD / $PLTR  as just two example, but my take is that the valuations of these rotations are reaching clown levels. And that certain AI supply chain beneficiaries in comparison are undervalued now. 

I was thinking markets would just rotate to names that are extremely profitable like Samsung or names that have <2X P/E, so it was surprising to see $KOSPI and some legacy memory players get sold off today. 

Since all of this is colliding with uncertainty about sht macro environments and renewed sustainability concern of AI capex/commitments from frontier labs like OpenAI/Anthropic from due to that FT piece recently. I've always been sounding the alarm about the contractual backlog OpenAI has with $CBRS, $MSFT, $ORCL and others earlier in the year. But OpenAI did just raise $122B or so , so I don't quite think they're at risk of going down anytime soon. 

I also don't think overall capex can just exponentially go up, but even if it stalls / hovers around a certain point or even drops...

Capex toward certain areas like optics will still explode as hyperscalers fight over allocations when CPO scale up comes about, but might drop in others where more capacity comes online like test or DRAM. So it's a lot more nuanced than capex down = everything down or vice versa.   

I also slightly agree with community agreements that open weight models wouldn't lessen demand on AI infrastructure (otherwise $NVDA wouldn't be funneling funds into Reflection), but all the contractual obligations that Anthropic has might get messy if their models/company get cannibalized. 

Either way, I'd expect some of these frontier lab valuations to likely compress but I do think Jensen knows what he's doing though to avoid contagion.

But basically: 

- Extremely difficult market now, can't just throw money at any AI supply chain company like $GLW and expect it to go up. There's cause for concern of rate hikes mixed with financing per $AVGO CEO but not to the point you just blindly sell off everything.

Also I think markets are stupid and ties baskets together so that leads to mispricing + individual buying opportunities with certain chokepoints too.

If capacity + demand is visible and forward p/e compresses like $AAOI to single digits off hundreds or thousands of percent growth from hyperscalers off $471m transceiver revenues and hundreds of thousands of monthly ELSFP capacity. Or $SIVE coming online with 100M+ laser capacity + multiple foundries with ASP hikes on lasers. I wouldn't lump them into other AI supply chain names in IP like $RMBS or others. 

My take is that AI supply chain beneficiaries with closer inflection points, demand visibility, and forward P/E compressing due to economic leverage would likely outperform medium term despite current volatility. 

TLDR: 
- Memory strongest risk/adjusted return with LTAs + pricing floors extending to 2030's + buybacks. 
- My opinion is that optical supercycle for 2027-2028 with CPO/NPO is going to look absurd relative to capacity coming online of smaller suppliers. 
- Overwhelming fundamentals/growth colliding with sht macro + media scares
- Markets are stupid and groups things in baskets and sells them all off together or buys overvalued names, creating short/long opportunities

I'd give a prayer to people on short term options given underlying drop + IV decline, but there could be a reversal... who knows. Most valuable thing right now is time.

@Rian_2026 Good question! Just some informal thoughts... there's three "moats" to look at for $SIVE:

- Capacity 
- Qualifications (especially for custom DFB lasers)
- Technological

1. For capacity, they're coming online with 100M+ CW DFB lasers Q4 2027 (global supply is roughly ~608M EML/CW lasers currently per Trendforce). 

Obviously by 2027 global capacity is going to grow a lot, with $AAOI, $AVGO (3x expansion), and others coming online.  

But if you extrapolate their 2:1 statement, that implies 300m lasers/year long term coming from their own supply + external foundries. 

This is incredibly valuable during a shortage that was quoted to be 3-5 years, and $LITE stating they already have demand visibility into 2031...

And when suppliers have started to qualify many more (eg. 5-7 vendors vs. 2-3 earlier) due to bottlenecks. 

I'm sure a lot of how they achieve that staggering amount is due to their manufacturing process/yields (which is a moat). 

2. For qualifications, if you look at 70mW/100mW pluggable lines with Chinese players, I'd argue this is more generic and moreso reverting back to a capacity  argument and manufacturing process to achieve those numbers. 

Custom DFB arrays that they've been working on with Ayar (they hinted at 2-3 others back in 2023 like Celestial) take years for optical i/o related things and would be a moat if they finish quals. 

So it's not quite something you can hot swap or design out really easily for $MTSI or another company. But of course cpo scale up and such is mass volume in 2028, and we're still H2 2026. 

3. People can always compare raw specs like power output, but it's probably way way more nuanced so easier to just point toward customer statements. 

With $JBL 1.6T LRO: "I think that there's the potential for a relatively dramatic moat with our LRO part…" from Jabil's EVP, especially related to power consumption. And $SIVE is my guess sole source in this line. 

Jabil is probably the most important testament to how their lasers perform in mass production scenarios maybe around Q2 next year. 

Ayar said something similar along the lines of "we couldn't do it without Sivers" for custom implementations.

$MU went from 16 to 26 strategic customer agreements in a single quarter, and now @elonmusk is calling Micron the reasonable one on future memory prices while its peers have been “extortionate.”

Those contracts now cover more than 35% of revenue through 2030, with about $150B in remaining performance obligations and $32B in customer commitments, mostly cash deposits. 

Customers are paying upfront to lock in memory supply years ahead, memory has never had visibility like this.

Every HBM bit takes 3 to 4 times the wafer capacity of standard DRAM, node migrations are slower and new cleanrooms take years. That keeps DRAM bit growth around the low 20s% through 2028, while AI capex, HBM content per accelerator and agentic workloads keep pushing demand higher.

The biggest knock on memory has always been the cycle. Boom, bust, repeat. Contracts like these are how you kill that argument, and Micron is clearly playing the long game here.

In the short term price follows sentiment, and sentiment on memory is awful right now. But in the long run price follows earnings, and these contracts lock in years of them.

Cerebras is trading more than 50% below where it opened on its first day, and I just couldn’t pass up this opportunity.

UBS sees revenue going ~25x by 2030 at 46% margins, and the stock trades at about 20x 2028 earnings. 

I keep saying this: the growth story for AI is inference.

Training a model is a big upfront project. Running it, every time someone asks a question or an agent takes a step, is a bill that never stops, and the agentic shift makes that bill much bigger. A single agent task can fire off dozens of model calls, and every one of them waits on the one before it. A few seconds of waiting per call turns into minutes per task.

Cerebras attacks that wait directly. 

A GPU keeps the model’s weights in HBM next to the chip and has to pull them across for every token it generates. Cerebras builds one chip out of an entire silicon wafer, about 46,000 mm² and 4 trillion transistors against roughly 1,600 mm² and 208 billion for NVIDIA’s two-die B200, and keeps 44GB of memory on the wafer itself. 

Less waiting on memory means more tokens per second for each user, which is exactly what an agent stuck in a loop of model calls needs.

GPUs are the best general-purpose factory ever built. 

Cerebras is a specialist tool for one job, fast inference, and that’s one of the fastest-growing jobs in AI.

The stock is still richly priced and could go lower, but this is a long bet I’m willing to take.

With BOTH the 10-year yields and the U.S. dollar rising, here is how to plan for the worst-case scenario. I've experienced this market scenario already in my life.

Markets kept making all-time highs for 4 - 5 months, and then a -57% crash happened in the markets. But rising yields and dollar rising does NOT crash the markets alone. Something UNDERNEATH is typically the trigger.

The 2026 - 2027 triggers would be:

1. Private credit - this is the scarier one in my opinion. Seven major platforms (Blue Owl, Apollo, Ares, BlackRock, and Blackstone) have capped or blocked investor withdrawals. $4.6 billion is trapped basically. 

2. Auto loan delinquencies hit a record - 5.5% at 90+ days, worse than 2008 peak (5.3%). The consumer is cracking at the bottom.

3. Commercial real estate is at record deliquicieis - office CMBS delinquiency at 12.3%, higher than 2008 crisis. 

4. Corporate bankruptcies at 16 year highs - 372 large filings through mid-2026. Small business bankrupties up 50% as well.

5. S&P 500 is looking a lie right now - every sector fell in Sept except for tech - banks, utilities, equal weight S&P 500, only a few BIG tech names are holding up the markets 

6. Six banks have failed in 2026 - small ones, but the most in any year this decade. 

I find that the pattern is the same throughout our history; rates stay high, something that was relying on cheap money can't handle it, then that thing breaks, the break spreads to other things, and by the time the Fed cuts rates to fix it, the damage is already done.

So how do you prepare for this since we cannot TIME a top?

1. Raise cash gradually - don't sell everything. Don't go all-in on a few names. Raise cash from work and you'll have the opportunity of a life time waiting for you when the dip comes

2. Buy the 10 year - a 5.35% risk free yield is the highest in 24 years. You can park cash in short term Treasuries (SHV, BIL, SGOV) and get paid 5%+ while you wait. My wife and I have started buying 10 year as well.

3. Watch the leaders, not the index - the S&P is being held up by 5-7 names. When $NVDA, $AAPL, $MSFT start breaking lower on volume, that's your signal the last pillar is cracking. The rest of the market is already weak.

4. Avoid the junk, or size appropriately - small caps, unprofitable tech, high debt companies, anything that needs to refinance soon. The Russell 2000 has a third of its constituents classified as zombie companies. These get destroyed when credit tightens.

5. Quality over momentum - if you're staying long, own companies with no debt, strong cash flow, and pricing power. Think $GOOGL, $AMGN, $BRK. Companies that don't need to borrow money at 5%+ don't care about rates.

6. Don't short the top - the market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent. In 2007 the S&P rallied 5% for 4 months after the 10Y peaked. Being early on a short is the same as being wrong. Can hedge with defensives instead and/or raise cash.

7. Have a plan before you need one - decide now what you'll do if the S&P drops 10%, 20%, 30%. Write it down. When panic hits, you execute the plan instead of making emotional decisions.

The goal isn't to predict the crash. It's to survive it with enough capital to buy the bottom and become a multi-millionaire.

**焦点**：市场对 AI 这条链的定价正在分化。 ORCL 、 META 、 CRM 升，而 AMAT 、 MU 、 ANET 、 CRWV 同日跌——资金买的是手握应用与现金流的一端，卖的是依赖资本开支落地的另一端。 AMD 逆势升1.90%，Semtech（ SMTC ）升2.67%，说明沽压并非笼罩整个半导体板块，而是直指存储与设备。消息面上，亚马逊将 META 的 AI 购物代理挡在站外，一端涉及广告位的存续，一端涉及电商闭环的缺口；此事与当日涨跌幅并无直接对应，仅作题材观察。此外，国际货币基金组织最新报告将「AI市场回调」与战争、债务并列为全球风险，与设备及存储链的持续沽压构成同一条叙事线。
